attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Psychiatry
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
History of mood swings with periods of elevated mood and increased productivity alternating with depressed mood

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She reports several episodes of feeling "on top of the world," during which she would start numerous projects, talk rapidly, and feel like she needed less sleep. These episodes last about 4 days and are followed by periods of intense sadness, fatigue, and disinterest in activities, lasting for more than 2 weeks.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
She denies any history of substance abuse or medical conditions.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
Her family history is significant for bipolar disorder in her mother.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She denies any history of substance abuse or medical conditions.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, she is well-groomed, her speech is rapid, and she appears to be easily distracted. Her mood is elevated, and affect is congruent. She denies any suicidal ideation or psychotic symptoms. Her physical examination is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory values:
- CBC: Normal
- Thyroid function tests: Normal
- Urine toxicology screen: Negative

attachments.title: Source clinical note

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Psychiatry
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Four-day history of increased energy, decreased need for sleep, and pressured speech

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the outpatient psychiatry clinic approximately eight months after her initial presentation for mood swings with periods of elevated mood and increased productivity alternating with depressed mood. She presents with a 4-day history of increased energy, decreased need for sleep, and more talkative than usual. She reports feeling "on top of the world" and has been more active on social media, posting several times an hour about her plans to start a new business, despite having no prior experience in the field. Her family reports that she has been spending money excessively and has been more irritable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Bipolar II disorder, current episode hypomanic (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

She has a history of major depressive episodes, the last one occurring six months ago.

MEDICATIONS:
She is not currently on any medications

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother with generalized anxiety disorder
- Maternal uncle with bipolar I disorder
- Paternal grandmother with major depressive disorder

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Marketing coordinator.

VITAL SIGNS:
Her vital signs are within normal limits

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, she is well-groomed, her speech is rapid, and she is easily distracted. She denies any hallucinations or delusions. the physical examination is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory values:
- Complete blood count (CBC): within normal limits
- Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH): within normal limits
- Urine toxicology screen: negative
